sources.citation: Courtois, Victor José. 1900. Elementos de grammatica tetense (lingua chi-nyungue), idioma fallado no districto de Tete e em toda a vasta região do Zambeze inferior. Nova edição. Coimbra: Imprensa da Universidade. xii+241 pp. (archive.org item elementosdegramm00couruoft)
sources.note: For the Tete language (Nyungwe): accent as a general rule on the penultimate syllable of every word; accent normally not written except where doubt could arise (kúsua 'quebrar' vs kusúa 'ter saudades'); verbs in -ua/-ia, passives in -iwa/-idua/-edua, contracted possessives (babache) and the enclitics -ni/-nyi all keep penultimate accent; separately, 'aspirated or accented' syllables distinguish words (kupa 'dar' vs kup'a 'matar'). Nothing on tone as such.

sources.note: Nothing. Only first-hand publication with Ɗema data (authors' fieldwork at Songo, Tete). Appendix p.177 'N403 Ɗema': Senaic, possibly closest to Nyungwe; p.180 'S101 Ɗoma' (Kanyemba, Shonic, close to N. Korekore) and notes that ISO dmx 'Dema' under Shona is a confusion of the two. Morphosyntax only; Ɗema appears only in tables (na; ɾi-ɓe). No tone/stress statement for Ɗema.
